title: Investigate and remediate token-throughput entropy spike affecting multi-model fanout
text:
Investigate and remediate token-throughput entropy spike affecting multi-model fanout

description:
Multiple customers reported sudden drops in tokens/sec and increased time-to-first-token (TTFT) after the runtime-1.21 rollout. The symptoms include bursty token emission (tokens/sec variance > 6x baseline) and sporadic TTFT spikes up to 4x on heterogeneous fanout (multi-model requests). Impact observed across Hosted API, Dedicated clusters, and a customer Private VPC. This ticket coordinates triage, customer communication, immediate mitigation, and a guarded fix rollout.

symptoms_and_evidence:
Observed increased TTFT and token-rate variance on redwood-medium-v1 and open-13b-quant variants starting 2026-03-09 03:20Z
Prometheus: rate(tokens_emitted[1m]) shows sawtooth pattern for affected nodes (query: sum by(node)(rate(redwood_tokens_emitted_total[1m])) )
SLO alerts: hosted-ttft-p50 breached for 3 enterprise customers (CustomerA, CustomerB, CustomerC)
Customer bridge logs: customer-reports/CR-9982 and CR-10009 with attached request traces and sample prompts

initial_actions_taken:
Opened incident bridge (channel #incident-ttft-entropy) and paged runtime and scheduler on-call
Rolled performance traces and flamegraphs for three representative requests (short-chat, long-context summarization, multi-turn instruction)
Scoped the regression window to runtime-1.21 kernel selector heuristic change via deploy timeline correlation

root_cause_summary:
A new kernel-selection heuristic in runtime-1.21 introduced probabilistic interleaving for microbatch kernel binding. Under heterogeneous fanout (different model sizes/quantizations per request), the heuristic occasionally groups incompatible microbatches causing repeated micro-kernel preemption and KV cache thrash. The preemption ripple reduced sustained token emission capacity and increased cold-path TTFT for affected nodes.

diagnostic_notes:
Reproducer: synthetic fanout workload that alternates 7B/13B/13B-quant requests at 20 qps replicates tokens/sec variance on canary cluster
Telemetry shows kernel_swap_count spiking before token-rate collapse (query: sum(rate(kernel_swap_total[5m])) by(machine))
KV cache hit-rate drops ~18% on affected nodes during events
Failure more pronounced on Dedicated clusters with mixed-priority placement and on Private VPCs that mirror tenant fanout patterns

fix_plan:
Immediate mitigation: flip kernel-selector heuristic flag to legacy behavior on 50% of capacity (canary) and 100% for critical customers; rollout controlled via flag runtime.config.kernel_heuristic_v2 = false
Medium-term: implement deterministic microbatch partitioning that enforces affinity rules for model size + quantization to avoid incompatible grouping
Add monotonic backoff for microkernel preemption and increase KV cache reservation credits during mixed fanout windows
Expand microbench tests to include heterogeneous fanout traces in CI performance suite

rollback_plan:
If canary shows customer TTFT improvement < 60% or new regressions appear, rollback runtime-1.21 kernel-heuristic changes using shipctl rollback command to runtime-1.20 snapshot. Notify SRE and pause automated rollout. Rollback schedule: canary -> 10min monitor -> 100% rollback if criteria met.

customer_communications:
2026-03-09 07:04Z: Short post to CustomerA bridge acknowledging impact and 'we're investigating'
2026-03-10 11:22Z: Sent mitigation update and temporary throughput knobs; offered rate-limited dedicated buffer while we remediate
2026-03-11 02:15Z: Informed enterprise customers of planned canary flip and expected 15-30 minute degraded window

dashboards_and_queries:
TTFT dashboard: /dash/ops/ttft-overview (filter: model=~(redwood-medium|open-13b).* )
PromQL sample: sum by(region)(rate(tokens_emitted_total[1m]))
Kernel swaps: sum by(machine)(increase(kernel_swap_total[5m]))

review_feedback:
PM (Lina Chen): prioritize customer-facing mitigation and put a kill-switch flag in the control plane
SRE (Jon Ortiz): add guardrail to autoscaler to avoid triggering mixed-priority placement when kernel heuristics are unstable
Lead Eng (Ravi Shah): prefer deterministic partitioning over probabilistic heuristics for long-term stability

next_steps:
Mateo: flip canary flag for kernel_heuristic_v2 -> false for 10% capacity and monitor (due 2026-03-12 09:00Z)
Anika: run CI heterogeneous fanout perf job and post results to the incident channel (due 2026-03-12 12:00Z)
SRE: prepare rollback runbook and validate automated rollback path (due 2026-03-12 10:30Z)
PM Lina: send customer status update after canary observation window (due 2026-03-12 11:00Z)

resolution_summary:


postmortem_notes:
Plan to schedule a full RCA and postmortem after stabilization window closes
Action: add heterogeneous fanout scenarios to pre-deploy performance gate for future runtime changes
Action: add metric 'microbatch_affinity_mismatch' and alert when >5% of microbatches are incompatible
